## Solution

We count the number of $\{+1,-1}$-assignments to an $m\times n$ grid such that every row product equals $-1$ and every column product equals $-1$.

### Consistency (parity) condition

Let $a_{ij}\in\{+1,-1\}$ be the entry in row $i$, column $j$. The product of all $mn$ entries can be computed two ways:

- **Row-wise:** $\prod_{i=1}^{m}\prod_{j=1}^{n} a_{ij} = \prod_{i=1}^{m}\underbrace{\left(\prod_{j=1}^{n}a_{ij}\right)}_{=-1} = (-1)^{m}.$
- **Column-wise:** $\prod_{j=1}^{n}\prod_{i=1}^{m} a_{ij} = \prod_{j=1}^{n}\underbrace{\left(\prod_{i=1}^{m}a_{ij}\right)}_{=-1} = (-1)^{n}.$

Since both equal the same product of all entries, we must have $(-1)^{m}=(-1)^{n}$, i.e.

$$m \equiv n \pmod{2}.$$

**If $m\not\equiv n\pmod{2}$, the constraints are inconsistent, so the answer is $0$.**

### Construction when $m\equiv n\pmod{2}$

We show the constraints are consistent and count the assignments.

**Free choices.** Assign values freely to the $(m-1)(n-1)$ entries in the upper-left $(m-1)\times(n-1)$ subgrid. Each of these $2^{(m-1)(n-1)}$ choices will be extended uniquely to a full valid grid.

**Determining the last column (rows $1,\dots,m-1$, column $n$).** For each $i\in\{1,\dots,m-1\}$, the row-product constraint $\prod_{j=1}^{n}a_{ij}=-1$ forces
$$a_{i,n} = -\prod_{j=1}^{n-1} a_{ij}.$$
This is a single determined value in $\{+1,-1\}$.

**Determining the last row (row $m$, columns $1,\dots,n-1$).** For each $j\in\{1,\dots,n-1\}$, the column-product constraint $\prod_{i=1}^{m}a_{ij}=-1$ forces
$$a_{m,j} = -\prod_{i=1}^{m-1} a_{ij}.$$
Again a single determined value.

**Determining the corner $a_{m,n}$.** The last-row constraint gives
$$a_{m,n} = -\prod_{j=1}^{n-1} a_{m,j},$$
and the last-column constraint gives
$$a_{m,n} = -\prod_{i=1}^{m-1} a_{i,n}.$$
We verify these agree. Computing the row-derived value:
$$a_{m,n}^{\text{row}} = -\prod_{j=1}^{n-1} a_{m,j} = -\prod_{j=1}^{n-1}\left(-\prod_{i=1}^{m-1}a_{ij}\right) = (-1)^{n}\prod_{j=1}^{n-1}\prod_{i=1}^{m-1} a_{ij}.$$
Computing the column-derived value:
$$a_{m,n}^{\text{col}} = -\prod_{i=1}^{m-1} a_{i,n} = -\prod_{i=1}^{m-1}\left(-\prod_{j=1}^{n-1}a_{ij}\right) = (-1)^{m}\prod_{i=1}^{m-1}\prod_{j=1}^{n-1} a_{ij}.$$
The two double products are identical, so the two values agree if and only if $(-1)^{n}=(-1)^{m}$, i.e. $m\equiv n\pmod{2}$ — which is exactly our standing assumption. Hence the corner is consistently determined, and every remaining row- and column-product constraint is satisfied by construction.

**Uniqueness.** Every valid assignment restricts to some choice on the upper-left $(m-1)\times(n-1)$ subgrid, and the above procedure shows that choice determines the entire grid. So the map "valid assignment $\mapsto$ its upper-left restriction" is a bijection onto all $2^{(m-1)(n-1)}$ subgrid assignments.

### Answer

$$\boxed{\text{Number of valid assignments} = \begin{cases} 2^{(m-1)(n-1)} & \text{if } m\equiv n \pmod{2},\\[4pt] 0 & \text{if } m\not\equiv n \pmod{2}. \end{cases}}$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
